limitations: This is a fixed two-case, six-run supplementary structural audit. It neither substitutes for the primary rubric nor defines a success gate; no arm identities were inferred.

Initial code and public contracts were read before initial scores were saved in crosscheck-work/initial-judgments.json. Maintenance code was first read only after MAINTENANCE_COMPLETE was observed. Author reports, private probes, primary grades, protocol, skill versions, baseline/candidate directories and other-agent sessions were not read.

An initial path inventory exposed filenames outside the fixed two-case sample; their contents were not opened or used. Subsequent reads were scoped to the authorized public originals and twelve frozen initial/maintenance pairs.

All tests were run only on disposable copies under crosscheck-work. Existing repository tests include author-added public tests; passing them is finite evidence, not an exhaustive independent behavioral proof. The original supplied test methods are AST-identical in every maintenance repository.

No new behavioral probes were invented. Numeric NaN/custom comparison objects, stateful item mappings or one-shot item iterators are not clearly specified by the public valid-input contract; guard inversion, any short-circuiting and repeated/eager item scanning could differ for such inputs. These are explicit scope ambiguities, not established contract failures and did not lower structural scores.

All ledger implementations now materialize calculated rows before CSV rendering. That is a real memory/traversal tradeoff versus emitting rows during the original calculation, but the public small-library goal specifies no streaming or scale requirement. No performance claim or penalty is made.

Only one maintenance change per case was observed. Results establish locality for these concrete changes, not arbitrary future changes. Identical scores reflect the coarse anchored rubric and coherent small solutions, not a preference for a particular helper count, pattern or file count.
